numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When one of X = U**(1/a) or Y = V**(1/b) underflows to 0 but the other does not, the code returns X/(X + Y), which is 0. This produces too many zeros (and too heavy a left tail) in beta samples. On the main branch the regression test counted nzeros = 133140 in its sample.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The logarithm-based calculation of X/(X + Y) should be used whenever either X or Y is 0, so the small but nonzero value is returned. The zero count should be close to the expected number of about 77616.9.
trigger_conditions: Beta distribution parameters a and b both less than 1, so Johnk's algorithm is used
Small a or b such that U**(1/a) or V**(1/b) underflows to 0 while the other does not (X or Y is 0 but X+Y > 0)
Small concentration parameters, e.g. a=0.0025, b=0.0025 in the regression test, with n=1000000 samples
Regression test test_beta_expected_zero_frequency counts zeros and checks 0.95*expected_freq < nzeros < 1.05*expected_freq (expected_freq=77616.90831318991)

input_output_examples.input: Beta sample with a=0.0025, b=0.0025, n=1000000 (regression test for gh-24475)

oracle_clues: Regression test test_beta_expected_zero_frequency asserts zero count within 0.95*expected_freq < nzeros < 1.05*expected_freq
Expected frequency computed with mpmath CDF of beta at smallest_subnormal/2 = 0.0776169083131899, per the numerical characteristics
Bounds were stated as not chosen with statistical rigor
Fix changes log-based branch in random_beta in numpy/random/src/distributions/distributions.c; at most ~1 ULP improvement per PR body

numerical_characteristics.precision: Discrepancy arises from underflow to 0 of U**(1/a) or V**(1/b) in double precision; values below machine epsilon / smallest subnormal are affected; the fix changes the log-based computation and yields at most ~1 ULP improvement in results
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Small concentration/beta parameters (alpha < 1, e.g. a=0.0025, b=0.0025 in regression test; alpha=0.005/2 in issue), where Dirichlet/beta components fall below machine epsilon
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: Regression test accepts nzeros within 0.95*expected_freq < nzeros < 1.05*expected_freq (expected_freq=77616.90831318991, n=1000000); bounds were stated as not chosen with statistical rigor
category_specific_evidence: Issue #24475: Dirichlet left tail too heavy at small alpha; too many zeros when alpha is low, values below machine epsilon.
Root cause: Johnk's algorithm in random_beta when both beta parameters are less than 1; X or Y underflows to 0 and code only used log-based calculation when both were 0.
Original buggy main branch gave nzeros = 133140 versus expected 77616.9.
Fix: use logarithm-based calculation if either X or Y is 0 (commit in distributions.c random_beta).
Regression test test_beta_expected_zero_frequency uses mpmath CDF of beta at smallest_subnormal/2 = 0.0776169083131899 to compute expected zero count.
Reference reproduction used numpy 1.25.2 on macOS arm64 with NEON; the stated versions are environment context only.
reproduction_risks: Zero-count test is stochastic and depends on seed; the 5% bounds were not statistically justified.
Expected frequency depends on mpmath high-precision CDF evaluation at x = smallest_subnormal/2; a double-precision computation would not reproduce it.
Counts depend on exact underflow behavior of U**(1/a) and V**(1/b), which may vary by platform and compiler (log/exp implementations).
Issue example compares against scipy loggamma, which the issue notes requires an up-to-date scipy.
